deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 12% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags

note.headline: NVIDIA closes 150.49 atop support as Huang-return and governance stories are reported

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is growing fast and makes a lot of cash, and the price already assumes about 19.1% starting cash-flow growth. That is cheap only if the 65.21% operating margin, the top of its 5-year range, holds.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, not add, because the margin and customer-payment risks are open. No swing trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: Buy at 117.15, trim near 226.93, wait on a close below 147.19

note.happening: NVIDIA closed at 150.49, up 0.8%. That sits just above the 147.19–150.41 support zone, the price area where buyers stepped in before. The trend is still down: the price is below its 20-day average of 169.32 and its 50-day average of 202.28, and both are falling. Today's news is commentary: CNBC and the FT reported on Jensen Huang's return and on an update to NVIDIA's code of conduct. Our data has no earnings date.
note.business: The numbers that drive the business are strong and improving. Last quarter's sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters ago. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left as operating profit, rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. NVIDIA has more cash than debt, with net cash of 23.2B. Analysts have raised next year's earnings estimate (EPS) by 27.7% over 90 days. The filings show three real risks. The margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and margins that high tend to fall back. Money customers owe but have not yet paid rose 127%, while sales rose 106%, both compared with a year earlier. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are stretched. Insiders also sold $946.6M of stock outside pre-set plans. Today's reported news on Huang's leadership and the code of conduct affects sentiment and governance only. Nothing in our data shows it changing demand, margins or cash. The shipment halt mentioned in the previous note's headline does not appear in today's news, so its effect on the business is still unknown. Demand and cash generation are not at risk based on the current numbers. The height of the margin and the quality of sales, given the slow customer payments, are at risk.

worth.text: At 150.49, the stock is valued at 18.9 times last year's earnings and 9.1 times next year's expected earnings. It trades at 12.0 times sales, below the peer median of 13.4 and in the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. A discounted cash flow model (DCF) values a company by projecting its future cash and converting it to today's money. Our DCF gives 194.8 in the bear case, 226.93 in the base case and 270.18 in the bull case. Valuing the stock on its own past price-to-sales levels gives 217.35 to 411.04. Every method lands above today's price. Working backward, the price implies free cash flow growth starting at 19.1%. At 20% starting growth the model gives 155.88, and at 10% it gives 105.42. Most of the gap between the methods comes from the margin. If the operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 117.15, and at 32% it drops to 78.42. So the stock looks cheap only if most of today's peak margin lasts.
worth.key_assumption: The operating margin stays near 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%, and free cash flow growth starts above the 19.1% the price implies.

No trade until a close above 171.5, the top of the resistance zone the price has hit 5 times.

decision.timing: Our data has no earnings date, and the options market prices a 14.7% move by 2026-12-18 with no earnings in that window. So the timing depends on the price holding 147.19 or breaking 171.5, not on the calendar.

change_mind: A close below 147.19 moves the long-term call from hold to wait, with the next support at 122.89–126.11.
A next filing with the operating margin back below 58.09%, or unpaid customer bills still growing faster than the 106% sales growth, would end the case for holding near 150.49.
